messages:
incidents-bot: PAGE: gpu-pool-eu-west nearing critical utilization (95%); queue growth observed for 18m. Autoscaler reported 'scale_limit_reached' twice. Paging on-call @alex and @maria. 

alex: picking this up. quick summary?

maria: saw the alert. queue length jumped from ~50 -> 120 in 10m, 429s to provider spiking. latency SLO breaches for a subset of tenants.

alex: logs? share the relevant query.

kevin: past 20m from collector: 
```
metric=gpu_pool_utilization region=eu-west-1 count=1 avg=0.95
metric=request_queue_length region=eu-west-1 count=1 avg=108
error=provider_429 rate=0.32 window=300s
autoscaler.event=scale_limit_reached reason=max_pools
```

jt_sre: autoscaler is hitting configured hard cap on pool count for eu-west-1 (max_pools=12). Looks like a sudden traffic fanout pushed us into parallel pool demand.

alex: can we create temporary extra capacity (bump max_pools) or failover to eu-central?

maria: infra has set max_pools deliberately low due to quota costs. ops-bot, any quick capacity injection?

ops-bot: We have standby capacity in eu-west-2 that can be rebalanced, but cross-region latency might be > 100ms for some customers. Manual approval required for immediate bump.

emily-cs: Customer impact: a few mid-market tenants report 5-10s extra latency and intermittent 503s. Support queue is getting DMs. Should prep customer comms.

alex: immediate mitigation checklist: 1) reduce per-request concurrency where safe, 2) enable degraded routing to eu-west-2 for non-SLA tenants, 3) drop heavy-batch inference to smaller batch sizes. Who can flip routing?

kevin: I can flip routing to eu-west-2 for the low-tier routing policy. Doing canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

maria: I'll lower default batch_size from 64 -> 32 for affected model endpoints (config flag). That reduces GPU memory pressure and may let more jobs fit per pool.

alex: jt_sre, can you temporarily raise max_pools to 16 while we assess? We'll roll back after stabilizing.

jt_sre: raising to 16 now. watch autoscaler logs.

deploy-bot: AUTO: routing-policy update applied (low-tier -> eu-west-2) by kevin.

kevin: canary at 10% applied. seeing small drop in eu-west queue. ramping to 50%.

alex: maria, batch size change applied?

maria: applied to 3 config groups. Observing GPU memory per pod drop ~18%. queue length dipping slowly.

incidents-bot: ALERT: queue length eu-west-1 decreased from 120 -> 40 over 8m. provider_429 rate falling.

alex: good. any residual customer-facing errors? emily-cs?

emily-cs: reduced, but a handful of enterprise tenants still show 2-3x latency. We need a post-incident note and possible credits. I'll prepare a draft once we have root cause.

kevin: can we confirm the autoscaler misread load pattern? logs show sudden spike in pod creation failures due to provider rate limits. Some pools failed to come online.

jt_sre: confirmed: provider-side throttle on instance creation caused backoff. Autoscaler kept retrying but hit our max_pools cap which prevented compensatory pools being created. This created a plateau: demand > available but autoscaler couldn't add more.

alex: root cause hypothesis: combined effect of provider quota spike + our conservative max_pools + large default batch sizes. Mitigations we did: emergency region spill, reduced batch, temporary max_pools bump.

maria: additional action: enable pre-warm pool feature for predicted daily spikes. We have a runbook for daytime ramp but it wasn't enabled for eu-west due to cost gating.

kevin: propose immediate action items: 
- restore max_pools to 12 (after cool-down) 
- request provider quota bump for instance creation rate in eu-west 
- enable pre-warm pool for 06:00-10:00 UTC for 1 week trial 
- add alert for "scale_limit_reached" that escalates earlier

alex: agree. also add: audit of batch_size by tenant type, and add a mitigation play to route non-enterprise traffic across regions automatically when pool saturation > 85%.

emily-cs: CS action: send initial incident ack to affected customers summarizing mitigations and ETA for RCA. I'll coordinate with legal on credits for enterprise tenants impacted.

jt_sre: creating a postmortem doc now. I'll include timeline and logs. We should capture exact provider 429 windows with timestamps.

maria: I'll attach the config diffs for batch_size and routing flags to the postmortem.

kevin: follow-up items for infra team: improve autoscaler behavior when provider creation fails (backoff jitter + alternative strategies), and consider soft-failover to cached model serving (cpu-only fallback) for low-sensitivity requests.

alex: who owns the quota request to cloud provider?

jt_sre: i'll open the request, assign to infrastructure procurement, and cc infra-ops. ETA 48-72h for initial increase.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: stabilized. on-call handover planned at +2h.

alex: logging handoff to @maria for next shift. Maria — you'll own postmortem and action tracking.

maria: acknowledged. I'll run through the playbook and draft the RCA. Expected postmortem draft in 24h.

emily-cs: I'll send a calm customer update now: short summary + actions taken + promise of RCA soon.

kevin: ops note: we should add a synthetic that simulates concurrent pool creation failure to test autoscaler resilience. Filed as ticket INFRA-987.

jt_sre: action items assigned: INFRA-987 (autoscaler resilience test), INFRA-988 (provider quota request), PLAT-452 (pre-warm pool enablement), DOC-3001 (runbook update for eu-west).

alex: thanks team. I'll keep monitoring for the next hour then sign off. If anything spikes, re-alert. :thumbsup: 

maria: posting summary to #postmortems when draft ready.

emily-cs: customers notified.

incidents-bot: THREAD CLOSED: stabilized -> monitoring.
